feed.title: NPR Topics: Climate
feed.subtitle: In-depth coverage of climate change, weather events, climate science, emissions targets and adaptation strategies from NPR’s climate reporters.

entry.title: After last year's storm, this remote Alaska town is still picking up the pieces
entry.summary: In October, 2025, the remnants of a typhoon seriously damaged Alaska Native villages in the far western part of the state. A year later, one of the hardest hit communities is still recovering.

entry.title: Halloween temperatures have been trending hotter. Here's what the data shows
entry.summary: Recent analysis from research nonprofit Climate Central found that on average, fall temperatures have warmed by 2.9 degrees Fahrenheit in the U.S. and the summer heat is lasting longer.

entry.title: Arizona's lifeline to the Colorado River is drying up. Its designers warned us decades ago
entry.summary: Arizona has now joined a lawsuit against the Trump administration's plan for sharing the Colorado River. But history shows water planners there saw big cuts to their water supply coming.

entry.title: Forecasters are predicting a warmer and wetter winter. Here's how El Niño will affect your region
entry.summary: El Niño years typically lead to more precipitation and higher-than-average temperatures. The latest data shows the different potential impacts by region.

entry.title: Trump administration wants to remove regulations on a super planet-heating gas
entry.summary: The Trump administration wants to undo a Biden-era rule that would reduce methane emissions from the oil and gas industry.

entry.title: Trump says he's ending restrictions on climate-warming methane from oil drilling
entry.summary: President Donald Trump said that his administration is "terminating" a Biden-era rule that aimed to cut planet-warming emissions of methane from oil and gas drilling.

entry.title: How AI is transforming hurricane forecasts
entry.summary: Hurricane forecasters are increasingly using artificial intelligence to make predictions.

entry.title: Flooding in Four Corners region displaces residents, as storms move southeast
entry.summary: Intense rainfall slammed the Four Corners region late this week. As rivers flooded, towns declared evacuations and emergencies and made rescues.

entry.title: Europe's heat claims 50,000 lives. Climate change blamed for two-thirds of deaths
entry.summary: Blistering record heat in Europe this summer helped kill more than 50,000 people, with nearly two-thirds of that death toll blamed on human-caused climate change, a new study found.

entry.title: UN warns world is on track to double global warming unless countries change course
entry.summary: The United Nations warns that countries are not meeting their goals to limit warming and avoid the worst consequences of climate change.
